newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat climbs on fund, commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat climbs on fund, commercial buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures were mostly higher at the midsession on a mixture of commercial- and fund-related buying in the May contract, traders said.

Cargill Investor Services had bought at least one million May bushels, and traders said this was linked to commercial business. Commodity brokers E. D. & F. Man International bought 1.5 million May, and Shay Grain bought 1.5 million July bushels.
"Commercial and fund buying has raced us higher," a KCBT trader said.
The surge allowed new crop July to climb off its opening lows, which came on ideas that recent moisture should help the HRW wheat crop when it emerges from dormancy.
At 1058 CST, KCBT wheat was one cent per bushel lower to six cents higher, with May up six cents at $4.01-3/4. March was up 1/4 cent at $4.19-1/2 and July was up three cents at $3.76.
